content.text: {"title":"AERO9500 Final Report (Part 2) - Space Mission Design","overview":"Design a simple space mission benefiting Australia and identify main elements of its space segment to demonstrate understanding of space segment systems (launch, orbits etc.) by developing a preliminary plan for a new mission using industry software and hand calculations.","deliverables":["Technical report as single PDF containing mission design and all related work","Relevant screenshots embedded in report or appendix","All relevant STK or PIGI design files included in report/appendix"],"format":{"length":"20 pages max for core part (excluding title page, table of contents, references, etc.), concise","structure":"Executive summary; Introduction - mission overview and rationale; Main body - all sections describing mission's space segment e.g. launch, orbit, ground stations, coverage, mission operation and end-of-life; Conclusion; Bibliography","other":"Engineering report writing style: clear, effective, correct grammar/spelling. Figures and tables fully and correctly labelled with number, title and reference if necessary. All non-original text/diagrams/ideas cited and referenced, plagiarism-checked; Wikipedia not a proper source. Include software outputs."},"requirements":[{"id":"R1","text":"Mission concept must benefit Australia in some way and be kept simple - examples: bushfire tracking and alert, weather satellite, internet/communication, earth observation for city planning/real estate."},{"id":"R2","text":"State spacecraft's primary mission."},{"id":"R3","text":"State whether using one or multiple spacecraft and justify."},{"id":"R4","text":"Identify users (operator and customers)."},{"id":"R5","text":"Define launch segment: where it will launch from and which launch vehicle."},{"id":"R6","text":"Define orbit segment: type of orbit, its characteristics and orbital elements."},{"id":"R7","text":"Determine if orbital maneuvers are required and detail them."},{"id":"R8","text":"Define ground segment: which ground control facilities will be used and how often spacecraft can communicate with ground control / coverage analysis."},{"id":"R9","text":"Define mission duration and plans for End-of-Life (EOL)."},{"id":"R10","text":"Use mission design software of choice to complete design (STK industry-standard, PIGI by Saber Astronautics - requires competition registration for license, or other like flightclub with prior approval) and supplement with hand calculations as needed."}]}
